elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 as rendered still provides that the Agreement "shall be automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — renewal is not by mutual written agreement, and the conditional preferred mechanics (30-day opt-out, 60-day vendor reminder) are not all satisfied, so the default is not displaced. To reach preferred, either condition renewal on the Parties' written agreement or add both the 30-day opt-out and the 60-day HDI reminder.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: "automatically renewed for an additional one year period on each anniversary of the Effective Date" — successive one-year (12-month) terms, no multi-year roll.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause requires "sixty (60) days written notice"; the preferred ceiling is 30 days. Defect: the operative number must read thirty (30) days for the Company's non-renewal notice to reach preferred.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: No reminder obligation appears anywhere in the rendered Section 4.1 or elsewhere in the cited text; the margin comment only mentions the reminder as part of the unattained preferred position. Defect: insert an operative obligation that HDI notify the Company in writing at least 60 days before each anniversary of the upcoming automatic renewal.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the only pricing term is the fixed formula in Section 3.1 ("thirty percent (30%) of the Net Sales in excess of Eleven Thousand Dollars ($11,000) per calendar month"), and Section 4.1 contains no renewal-uplift or repricing mechanic, so no price increase is permitted on renewal and the cap is not triggered.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 4.1: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon sixty (60) days written notice to the other" — 60 days, exactly at the fallback ceiling (down from ninety (90) days). The deterministic check reporting "number not found" is a detector miss: the digits "60" are present in the operative sentence and the window computes to 60 days.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no renewal price-escalation language exists; compensation stays at the fixed Section 3.1 revenue share. Note the mapping labels this "already_met" citing Section 3.1, which is a fee formula rather than a cap — the correct basis is that the condition is not triggered, but the outcome is the same.

reasons: Fallback is complete: the notice window now reads sixty (60) days (≤ 60) and no renewal price-uplift mechanic exists, so the 5% cap element is satisfied by inapplicability. The clause therefore lands at the fallback and the deviation is cured.

Preferred remains unmet on three elements: the opt-out notice is 60 rather than ≤ 30 days, there is no HDI reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and consequently the mutual-written-agreement default is not displaced. These are correctly characterised in the rationale as gaps short of preferred, not separate deviations.

Minimal: the sole edit is the numeral change from "ninety (90)" to "sixty (60)" in Section 4.1. Favourable existing language (one-year renewal term, bilateral structure, Termination Date definition) is retained, nothing is duplicated, and no requirement outside the fallback checklist is added.
Intent preserved: Section 3.1 economics, the Effective Date trigger, the Termination Date definition and the Section 4.2 Termination Payment all survive unchanged and without contradiction.

Watch-out (not a defect in this rule): Section 4.1's notice is bilateral, so the edit also shortens HDI's own exit notice from 90 to 60 days, reducing our transition runway. If the longer vendor notice is valued, bifurcate the sentence — e.g. "unless terminated by the Company upon sixty (60) days written notice, or by HDI upon ninety (90) days written notice" — which would still satisfy the fallback while retaining the favourable 90-day vendor exit notice.

Deterministic evidence reviewed in substance: the failing "non-renewal notice window ≤ 60 days" check is a false negative against the spelled-and-parenthesised form "sixty (60) days written notice"; the minimality and element-coverage gates pass and are consistent with the rendered text.
